title: Renewal as Risk Reduction: A Comparative Framework for Integrating Hazard Exposure into the Renewal of Ageing Infrastructure in Switzerland and the United States
content: Much of the transport infrastructure in Switzerland and the United States was built in the second half of the twentieth century and is now reaching the end of its design life, while its exposure to landslides, debris flows, rockfalls and floods is changing. This paper presents a structured comparative review of how the two countries account for natural-hazard exposure when renewing existing roads and bridges in mountain and hillslope environments. Following a PRISMA-guided search of OpenAlex, supplemented by targeted searches of Swiss and US institutional sources and citation searching, covering 2003-2026, 50 sources were included and coded along five predefined dimensions. Switzerland operates under an explicitly risk-based national strategy and a dedicated series of standards for existing structures (SIA 269). The United States relies on risk-based but condition-driven asset management and event-triggered hazard products, with some state agencies going beyond federal requirements. In both countries, hazard and climate risks are addressed at strategic or network level, but no uniform asset-level procedure requires a reassessment of changing exposure when an undamaged asset is renewed. The paper proposes a four-element framework (hazard-aware condition assessment, consequence-based prioritisation, integration of protective and functional infrastructure, and threshold-linked monitoring) and a five-step screening procedure for portfolio-level application. It identifies transferable practices, offers recommendations for agencies with limited capacity, and sets out an agenda for empirical validation.
